correctness.rationale: A partial isomorphism pairs nonempty selected intersections of original blocks of equal selected size, and extends exactly when each pair also agrees in original capacity: then complete the partial bijections and match unused blocks by capacity. An unequal-capacity pair needs at least δ omissions on its larger side. At n−δ equality forces the larger block of size t=s+δ to be cut to s, with no other omissions on that side. The other side has the same selected profile and hence an excess block of size s; creating it from a larger block also costs at least δ, forcing a single truncation from t to s on that side too. Distinct nearest pairs give disjoint profiles. For each pair the ordered domain/image choices number m_t² binom(t,δ)², and for each such choice there are g(m_s+1)s!/(m_t t!) isomorphisms. Exactly 1/(m_s+1) match the two truncated blocks and extend, giving the frozen count when summed over pairs. For A_E, D_α counts subsets of each selected-size profile; each ordered pair of such subsets contributes ∏_j a_j!(j!)^{a_j}. For R_E repeat independently within each original capacity s; each subset count is m_s!∏_{j≥1}binom(s,j)^{a_j}/∏_{j≥0}a_j!, and pairing only nonempty intersections cancels one factor a_j! for j≥1, leaving (a_0!)² as in the formula. This includes the empty map and all equal-capacity hosts. The example (1,3) gives 9 bad maps at rank 2, the largest bad rank, not the first in ascending order. Independent enumeration through n=7 compared both polynomials against direct partial injections and distinct restrictions of actual full automorphisms for 45 partition types, including the empty host.
residual_risks: Finite enumeration is only corroboration; the class-matching and omission arguments prove the unrestricted finite-host result.

evidence: The extendible profile factors into known equal-capacity pieces; the two-class defect formula is covered by the biclique result. Equal-capacity results cannot represent maps crossing original capacities, and a two-block statement alone does not rule out competing truncations in larger hosts.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The arbitrary first-defect formula needs the proof that both sides truncate a block from the same nearest-size pair, then a count allowing all m_s full s-blocks to compete with the truncated block. Decomposing the restrictions group or importing a two-class cutoff does not establish this rigidity or count.

evidence: An equivalence relation corresponds to the graph with a clique on each class (the diagonal is irrelevant). Complementing a disjoint union of two cliques gives K_{a,b}, preserving both induced partial isomorphisms and full automorphisms, hence also extendibility. The indexed biclique record gives precisely P_aP_b and the nonextendible polynomial C(C+2), cutoff 2b for a>b, and boundary count binom(a,b)²(b!)².
The equal-clique case in cd9dfc7a9f4c is exactly the equal-capacity case. In 23acc2a81818 'rank' instead measures recursive one-point extensions.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The biclique relation is an exact reduction, not just a match of parameters or coefficients. The present formula agrees since (a+b)−(a−b)=2b and a!b! binom(a,a−b)/(a−b)!=binom(a,b)²(b!)². Neither that reduction to bicliques nor the homogeneous theorem handles arbitrary capacity multisets.

value.rationale: The nearest gap identifies the exact robustness of host-level extension under omission, and the coefficient distinguishes how often extension first fails among nearly complete partial symmetries. Knowing only homogeneous behavior, two-class examples or that some low-rank map fails does not give that near-total census when the host has multiple capacities and repeated closest gaps. The coupled profiles give an exact way to compare all partial symmetries to the restrictions of global ones.
residual_risks: Scope is one finite equivalence relation, not ordinal extension rank, larger-host extension, or additional structure.
